card.name: Isukuti
card.tagline: Luhya drum dance, UNESCO urgent-safeguarding heritage
card.profile: Isukuti is a fast-paced, energetic celebratory dance of the Isukha and Idakho communities (Luhya) of Western Kenya, accompanied by drumming and singing (UNESCO). The dance derives its name from the isukuti drums, played in sets of three (big, medium and small) and accompanied by an antelope horn and metal rattles; a soloist leads thematic songs as dancers form separate rows for men and women. It permeates childbirths, initiations, weddings, funerals, inaugurations and religious festivities.
card.insight: In 2014 UNESCO inscribed the Isukuti dance on the List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding, warning that transmission is weakening as bearers age and younger generations turn to more commercial genres (UNESCO).
